finding.text: All four asks are met: one fragment (`ext/Refine/RefineStyle.js`), wired into the outline (Server/refine.mjs:351), asks (Server/refine.mjs:480) and Haiku notes (Servex/ext/refine/Annotator.js:26) prompts, a fixture test, and a doc linked from the readme. It's small and plain; I don't see a simpler shape.

Heading rule conflict: RefineStyle.js:22 says "#" for the subject and "##" for each part, but CLAUDE.md commit 313a0afd9 (same day) says "###" is the default and "##" is skipped. The brief asked for H2/H3, and Outline.parse plus the existing outline prompt (Server/refine.mjs:304, 325) are built on "#"/"##". Keeping "##" for outlines is right. One line saying "outlines use ##; chat replies follow CLAUDE.md" in doc/refine-style-2026-10-12.md would stop the next agent from "fixing" it.

The Haiku notes prompt (Annotator.js:26) now carries the whole RULES block: headings, ✅/⬜ bullets, [S#] cites. Its output is JSON alternates/names/tags, so only the "reuse names" line applies; the rest adds tokens to every batch call and could confuse it. A shorter `RefineStyle.NAMES` line for `for("notes")` would be enough.

I could not run test/refine-style.mjs in the worktree: it has no Servex/node_modules, and Server/refine.mjs imports ask-each.mjs statically, which needs the SDK. So the first check crashes with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND before any PASS/FAIL line. The doc says as much, but test/refine-style.mjs:28 and :34 should catch that error and SKIP, like the notes check at :41 does. Read by hand, the asserted counts look right: 5 problems for the rant-shaped outline, 3 sections, cites "1,2".

As doc/refine-style-2026-10-12.md says itself, no real-model run yet: whether Sonnet now reorders by dependency without dropping sentence coverage is untested. The first real refine run should be checked with `RefineStyle.check`.
